mainTopic: Does רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' mean fitness to eat the meat (היתר אכילה) or fitness to sprinkle the blood (היתר זריקה)? Also, what can an improper זריקה do for מעילה?
overview: The גמרא is asking what kind of 'fitness' רבי יהושע meant in the משנה. He said that once an offering had a time of fitness for the כהנים, it is no longer subject to מעילה. Did he mean the meat became permitted to eat (היתר אכילה), or only that the blood was ready to be sprinkled (היתר זריקה)? First the גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון about נותר, and then a matching one about פיגול. In both, 'before זריקה' there is מעילה and 'after זריקה' there is none. The גמרא tries to prove from these that fitness for sprinkling is not enough. Each time the proof is pushed away: רבי שמעון's words can mean 'before or after it was fit for זריקה'. A third proof, from פיגול of קדשי קדשים, is also turned aside. The גמרא then explains why that ברייתא contrasts קדשי קדשים with קדשים קלים. An improper זריקה, like one done with פיגול intent, can take an offering out of מעילה, but only a proper זריקה can bring something into מעילה.

steps.title: A teaching of רבי שמעון: two kinds of נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says some נותר is subject to מעילה and some is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says there is a case of נותר where one is liable for misusing it, and a case of נותר where one is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to help answer its open question. Right now it only quotes the opening line, and the explanation comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר is meat left past its allowed time, which makes it forbidden. רבי שמעון says this one status can go either way when it comes to מעילה. That split is the key the גמרא will use to work out what 'fitness' means in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time, which makes it forbidden
One is liable for misusing קדשים (sacred property)
The sin of using sacred property for personal benefit

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Shimon says:
There is notar for which one is liable for misuse,
and there is notar for which one is not liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source for the ongoing question of היתר אכילה versus היתר זריקה
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of 'fitness to the כהנים' in רבי יהושע's statement

steps.title: How the two kinds of נותר differ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that if the meat was left overnight before זריקה there is מעילה, and after זריקה there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If it was left overnight before the sprinkling, one is liable for misuse. If it was left overnight after the sprinkling, one is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out its two cases. Everything depends on whether the blood was sprinkled before the meat became נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood is sprinkled, the meat becomes permitted to the כהנים, and that removes it from מעילה. Even if it later becomes נותר, the מעילה does not come back. If the blood stayed overnight before any sprinkling, the offering became unfit and never left the category of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces the explanation)
Was left overnight
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נותר after זריקה stops being נותר. It is still forbidden to eat. It is only free of the separate sin of מעילה.

phrases.english: How so?
If it was left overnight before the sprinkling, one is liable for misuse;
if after the sprinkling, one is not liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two cases introduced in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נותר before זריקה is subject to מעילה; נותר after זריקה is not

steps.title: Even when there was time to sprinkle, מעילה remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי שמעון's first case includes a situation where there was time to sprinkle, and still there is מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, he teaches that one is liable for misuse. Isn't this even where there was time to sprinkle it, so that if he had wanted, he could have sprinkled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out the hidden point in the ברייתא. The case of 'before sprinkling' seems to include a time when sprinkling was fully possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood could have been sprinkled, the offering had a time when it was fit for זריקה. Even so, רבי שמעון still says there is מעילה. So fitness for sprinkling alone does not remove מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (focuses on one detail of the source)
Enough time
If he wanted

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches: one is liable for misusing it.
Is it not where there was time to sprinkle it,
so that if he wanted, he could have sprinkled?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת: מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ, לָאו דַּהֲוָה שְׁהוּת לְמִיזְרְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads a hidden detail into the first case of the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: Whether fitness for זריקה removes מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'before זריקה' case in רבי שמעון's ברייתא

steps.title: So the משנה means fitness for eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' means the meat was permitted for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from this: it is fitness for eating that we learned in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the proof. The 'fitness' in the משנה is היתר אכילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed that fitness for sprinkling alone does not end מעילה. So the only fitness that does end it is when the meat actually became permitted to eat. That is what רבי יהושע meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (introduces a conclusion)
The meat being permitted to eat

steps.whatToRemember: According to this proof, an offering leaves מעילה only once its meat became permitted to eat (היתר אכילה). Fitness for sprinkling (היתר זריקה) is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the claim the rest of the sugya tests. If it holds, an offering leaves מעילה only when the meat actually becomes permitted, not when it merely could have been. The very next step pushes this proof away.

phrases.english: And learn from this:
It is fitness for eating that we learned!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יהושע's words in the משנה about an offering that had a time when it was fit for the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the inference in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the proof suggests that 'fitness to the כהנים' in רבי יהושע's statement means היתר אכילה, not היתר זריקה. Step 5 pushes this proof away.

steps.title: No: the blood was collected too close to sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי שמעון's first case is where the blood was collected so close to sunset that there was no time to sprinkle it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where he collected the blood close to sunset, so there was no time to sprinkle it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 3. It says the ברייתא is not talking about a case where there was time to sprinkle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 claimed that רבי שמעון gives מעילה even when there was time to sprinkle, which would prove that fitness for זריקה does not matter. Now the גמרא limits his case to blood collected just before sunset, when זריקה was impossible. So the meat never became fit for זריקה, and the מעילה tells us nothing against that view.

keyTerms.meaning: sunset; after it, blood can no longer be sprinkled
enough time to do something
collecting the blood of the offering in a vessel

phrases.english: No,
where he collected it close to sunset,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the blood of the offering, which the כהן caught in a vessel.

phrases.english: so there was no time to sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 3-4 by narrowing רבי שמעון's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' must mean fit for eating.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי שמעון's case included time to sprinkle, but it can be limited to a case with no such time.

steps.title: So if there was time, would there be no מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out what the new reading means: if there had been time to sprinkle, there would be no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there was time, what is the law? Would there then really be no מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what follows from the answer just given. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is limited to 'no time to sprinkle,' then the opposite case, where there was time, should have no מעילה. The גמרא accepts this result for now, but it leads straight into a question about רבי שמעון's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: one is liable for מעילה, misusing sacred property
so too / indeed so

phrases.english: But if there was time, what is the law?
So too, would one not be liable for misuse?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָיָה שְׁהוּת, מַאי? הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵין מוֹעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of the limited case in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the law is when there was time to sprinkle, according to the reading in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The implied answer is that there would be no מעילה, and the next step builds a challenge on that.

steps.title: Then why did רבי שמעון say 'before זריקה' and not 'before sunset'?
steps.stepSummary: If time to sprinkle is what counts, רבי שמעון should have divided the cases by sunset, not by whether זריקה actually happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he teach 'before זריקה'? He should have taught 'before sunset' and 'after sunset'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from רבי שמעון's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the reading in Step 5, what matters is whether there was still time before sunset to sprinkle, not whether the blood was actually sprinkled. So 'before זריקה' and 'after זריקה' seem like the wrong way to divide the cases. Dividing by sunset would have been more exact.

keyTerms.meaning: why specifically? (why choose this wording?)
let him teach (he should have said)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Before sunset' here means the blood was collected while there was still time to sprinkle it that day. 'After sunset' means it was too late to sprinkle.

phrases.english: Why specifically does he teach 'before sprinkling'?
Let him teach 'before sunset' and 'after sunset'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of Step 6 to attack the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 5, which limits רבי שמעון's case to no time to sprinkle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If time to sprinkle is the key factor, the ברייתא's wording 'before/after זריקה' does not match. It should have said 'before/after sunset.'

steps.title: He meant before and after it was fit for זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's words mean 'before it was fit for זריקה' and 'after it was fit for זריקה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he teaches: before it was fit for זריקה, and after it was fit for זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רבי שמעון's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Before זריקה' does not mean before the actual sprinkling. It means before the blood was fit to be sprinkled. Once that reading is accepted, the ברייתא fits the view that fitness for זריקה is what matters, and the proof from Steps 3-4 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: that it becomes fit for sprinkling
he is teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's 'before/after זריקה' can mean 'before/after it was fit for זריקה.' So his ברייתא does not prove that רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' means fit for eating.

phrases.english: That is indeed what he teaches:
before it is fit for sprinkling,
and after it is fit for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before זריקה' means before the blood was actually sprinkled.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Before זריקה' means before the blood was fit to be sprinkled, so the ברייתא fits the view that fitness for זריקה is what matters.

steps.title: A new source: רבי שמעון on פיגול and מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון: some פיגול offerings carry מעילה and some do not. Before זריקה there is מעילה. After זריקה there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says, there is a פיגול offering that carries מעילה, and there is a פיגול offering that does not. How so? Before the blood is sprinkled, there is מעילה. After it is sprinkled, there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a second source to try to answer the same question as before. Here it only quotes the source; the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an offering that became פיגול is still holy property, so taking it is מעילה. רבי שמעון teaches that the dividing line is זריקה: once the blood is sprinkled, מעילה ends.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid because the כהן had the wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Using holy property for your own benefit
One is liable for מעילה if he uses it
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
How so? An opening to explain a general statement

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Shimon says:
There is a piggul offering for which one is liable for misuse,
and there is a piggul offering for which one is not liable for misuse.
How so?
Before the sprinkling, one is liable for misuse;
after the sprinkling, one is not liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned aside in steps 5-8, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' means fitness for eating or fitness for זריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ברייתא dividing פיגול into before זריקה (מעילה) and after זריקה (no מעילה)

steps.title: The proof: there was time to sprinkle and still there is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'before זריקה' as a case where the כהן had time to sprinkle and simply did not. Since there is still מעילה, fitness for זריקה is not enough. So רבי יהושע must mean fitness for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, he teaches that before זריקה there is מעילה. Isn't this a case where there was time to sprinkle, so if he wanted he could have sprinkled? And still he teaches there is מעילה. Learn from this: we learned 'permitted for eating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of רבי שמעון's words and reaches a conclusion. 'Time of fitness' means the meat was permitted to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being ready for זריקה were enough to end מעילה, then 'before זריקה' with time to sprinkle should have no מעילה. רבי שמעון says there is מעילה. So readiness for זריקה is not what ends מעילה, and the גמרא concludes that רבי יהושע meant היתר אכילה.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches; focusing on the one part of the source that matters
Enough time left in the day
To sprinkle it (the blood)
Learn from it; a conclusion is drawn
Permission to eat the meat

phrases.english: In any event, he teaches:
before the sprinkling, one is liable for misusing it.
Is it not where there was time to sprinkle it,
so that if he wanted, he could have sprinkled?
And still he teaches, 'one is liable for misusing it.'
So learn from it:
it is permission to eat that we learned!
phrases.notes: Again, this points back to רבי יהושע's words in the משנה about a 'time of fitness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the actual proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now: רבי יהושע's 'time of fitness' means the meat was permitted for eating, not just ready for זריקה.

steps.title: Rejected: the case is where there was no time to sprinkle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. רבי שמעון's 'before זריקה' can be a case where there was no time left to sprinkle the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is where there was no time to sprinkle it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the case differently, just as it did with the first proof in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was no time to sprinkle, the offering was never even fit for זריקה. Then there is מעילה either way, and the ברייתא proves nothing about whether fitness for זריקה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: No; the proof is being rejected
Where there was not
Pushing away a proof by reading the case another way

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the גמרא has decided that fitness for זריקה is enough. It only shows the ברייתא can be read another way, so it is no proof.

phrases.english: No,
it is where there was no time to sprinkle it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא, not the idea that 'time of fitness' means eating.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed there was time to sprinkle; the case can be one where there was not.

steps.title: Then if there was time to sprinkle, is there no מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out what the new reading means: where there was time to sprinkle, the offering would already be out of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there was time to sprinkle it, what? Would it really be out of מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the rejection means, setting up a challenge that will come next, just as in steps 6-7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'before זריקה' only means 'no time to sprinkle,' then where there was time, there should be no מעילה even without sprinkling. The גמרא is checking whether that idea fits רבי שמעון's words.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the law?
So too; would it really be so?
It has left the status of מעילה

phrases.english: But if there was time to sprinkle it, what?
Would it really have left the status of misuse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the meaning of the rejection in step 11 and prepares a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, under the new reading, an offering with time left to sprinkle is already free from מעילה.

steps.title: Why not say before and after sunset?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון's line depends on whether there was time to sprinkle, he should have said 'before sunset' and 'after sunset' instead of 'before/after זריקה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he specifically say 'after זריקה'? Let him say 'before sunset' and 'after sunset'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from steps 11-12. If what matters is whether there was time to sprinkle, the wording 'before/after זריקה' seems like the wrong way to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the גמרא said 'before זריקה' means there was no time left to sprinkle. If time is the real point, the clear line is sunset, because blood not sprinkled by sunset becomes unfit. So why did רבי שמעון talk about זריקה at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (Why say it this way?)
Sunset
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Why does he specifically teach "after sprinkling"?
Let him teach "before sunset"
and "after sunset"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording behind the reading given in steps 11-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי שמעון's 'before/after זריקה' depends on whether there was time to sprinkle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If time to sprinkle is the real line, sunset would be the clearer way to say it.

steps.title: That is what he means
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's words really do mean 'before it was fit for זריקה' and 'after it was fit for זריקה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying: before it is fit for זריקה, and after it is fit for זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'before/after זריקה' is simply short for 'before/after it became fit for זריקה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not change the reading. It explains that 'זריקה' in רבי שמעון's words means the point when the blood was ready to be sprinkled. That covers the time question without needing to mention sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what he means
When it becomes fit for sprinkling

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying:
before it is fit for sprinkling,
after it is fit for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before/after זריקה' seemed to mean the actual act of sprinkling, so sunset would have been clearer.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Before/after זריקה' means before or after it became fit for sprinkling, so the wording works.
steps.whatToRemember: Proof from רבי שמעון is pushed off. His words can mean that fitness for זריקה is what matters.

steps.title: A new proof from פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says פיגול in קדשי קדשים still has מעילה. If this means even after זריקה, then what removes מעילה is היתר אכילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: פיגול of קדשי קדשים — one is liable for מעילה. Isn't this where he sprinkled? Learn from it that we were taught about permission to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to show that רבי יהושע means permission to eat the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול meat can never be eaten. If the ברייתא means that פיגול keeps מעילה even after זריקה, then זריקה alone does not remove מעילה. What removes it must be the meat becoming permitted to eat, and פיגול never reaches that point.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made unfit by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
The most holy offerings
One is liable for מעילה (misusing holy property)
Permission to eat the meat

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Piggul among the most holy offerings: one is liable for misuse.
Is it not talking about where he sprinkled the blood?
And learn from it:
It is permission to eat that we learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי שמעון fails, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע's 'time of being permitted' means היתר אכילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: פיגול in קדשי קדשים is subject to מעילה, read as being after זריקה.

steps.title: Maybe the blood was not sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא can be talking about a case where the blood was not yet sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he did not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof away by reading the ברייתא as a case before זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood was never sprinkled, then of course there is מעילה, no matter what view we hold. So the ברייתא no longer shows that זריקה is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he did not sprinkle

phrases.english: No, it is where he did not sprinkle.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was talking about after זריקה, but it could be before.

steps.title: Then why contrast קדשים קלים?
steps.stepSummary: If after זריקה פיגול has no מעילה, why does the ברייתא single out קדשים קלים as having no מעילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he sprinkled, what? Is it indeed that there is no מעילה? Then why does it specifically teach that with קדשים קלים there is no מעילה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge the answer of step 16. The challenge continues into the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is talking about before זריקה, then after זריקה even פיגול of קדשי קדשים would have no מעילה. If so, why did the ברייתא bring קדשים קלים as its example of no מעילה? It could have shown the difference inside קדשי קדשים itself, as the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness
There is no liability for מעילה with it

phrases.english: But where he did sprinkle, what?
Is it indeed that there is no misuse with it?
Why does it specifically teach
that with offerings of lesser holiness there is no misuse with it?

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the פיגול ברייתא is talking about before זריקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If after זריקה קדשי קדשים would also have no מעילה, the ברייתא should have taught the no-מעילה case within קדשי קדשים (before versus after זריקה) instead of switching to קדשים קלים.

steps.title: The ברייתא should have said 'before sprinkling' and 'after sprinkling'
steps.stepSummary: If after זריקה a פיגול offering has no מעילה, the ברייתא could have made its distinction inside קדשי קדשים: before זריקה there is מעילה, after זריקה there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the ברייתא teach it this way: here, before the sprinkling; there, after the sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from the last step. It suggests the wording the ברייתא should have used if the rule really depends on whether the blood was sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasted two kinds of offerings: קדשי קדשים have מעילה and קדשים קלים do not. The גמרא asks why it did not use a simpler contrast within קדשי קדשים alone, between before זריקה and after זריקה. That would show directly that זריקה is what removes מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach. The גמרא suggests a better way the ברייתא could have worded its ruling.
Sprinkling the offering's blood on the מזבח.
Before / after.

phrases.english: Let it teach: here, before the sprinkling,
phrases.notes: He means: let the ברייתא teach both cases about קדשי קדשים alone.

phrases.english: there, after the sprinkling!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִיתְנֵי: כָּאן – לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה, כָּאן – לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 17 by proposing the alternative wording the ברייתא should have used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the ברייתא is worded, contrasting קדשי קדשים with קדשים קלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the real difference is whether זריקה happened, a before/after contrast would be clearer than a contrast between two kinds of offerings.

steps.title: Improper sprinkling can remove מעילה but cannot create it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא chose its wording to teach a rule. When זריקה would bring something into מעילה, only a proper זריקה does it. When זריקה would take something out of מעילה, even an improper זריקה does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to teach us: wherever the sprinkling would bring something into מעילה, only a proper sprinkling brings it into מעילה. Wherever the sprinkling would take something out of מעילה, even an improper one also takes it out of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's wording teaches an important rule about what a flawed sprinkling can and cannot do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים קלים, זריקה is what makes the parts burned on the מזבח subject to מעילה. A פיגול זריקה is improper, so it cannot create מעילה, and that is why the ברייתא says there is none. In קדשי קדשים, זריקה is what removes מעילה, and even an improper זריקה can do that, so the ברייתא's case of מעילה there must be before the זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach us. A new point is being taught.
The sin of making personal use of הקדש, holy property.
To bring in. Here, to make something subject to מעילה.
To take out. Here, to remove something from מעילה.
Done properly / done improperly.
Removes, cancels.

steps.whatToRemember: A flawed זריקה is weak. It can take an offering out of מעילה, but it cannot bring an offering into מעילה. That is why פיגול קדשים קלים never become subject to מעילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the same פיגול זריקה is 'good' in one case and 'bad' in the other. It is always improper. The point is that removing מעילה needs less than creating it.

wherever it is to bring something into מעילה,
phrases.notes: This is the case of קדשים קלים. Their parts that go on the מזבח only get מעילה after the זריקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by explaining that the ברייתא's chosen contrast teaches a rule a before/after contrast would not.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the ברייתא's wording: it is teaching an extra rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The before/after contrast would have been simpler, so the ברייתא's wording looks unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording teaches that an improper זריקה, such as פיגול, can remove מעילה but cannot bring an offering into מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why פיגול affects the two kinds of offerings differently. It also confirms that for קדשי קדשים, even a פיגול זריקה ends מעילה.
